project.name: Demo: Clinic Queue
project.idea: A walk-in clinic queue app: patients take a token from a kiosk or their phone, see live wait times, and get an SMS when the doctor is ready.

phases.summary: Must-haves: token issue, live queue, SMS call-in. v2: multi-doctor routing, no-show handling.
Next.js + Postgres + Twilio. 3 sprints / 60 pts. CFO abort at 5 sprints.
Contract B: 11 files, 4 entities. Contract C ordered. Consistency gate ✓.

requirements.text: Issue a numbered token from the kiosk
Live queue board with estimated wait
SMS the patient when they are next
Patients can take a token from their phone (QR at the door)
Receptionist can skip / recall a token
Route tokens to a specific doctor
Daily report: patients seen, average wait

sprints.goal: Foundation: schema, token issue, queue board

stories.title: Twilio SMS when patient is next
E2E: take token → called by SMS

A.original_requirements: A walk-in clinic queue app with tokens, live wait times and SMS call-in.
A.product_goals:
Cut perceived waiting time
Zero receptionist effort for the happy path
Works on a cheap Android tablet kiosk
A.user_stories:
As a patient, I want a token so that I know my place in line
As a patient, I want an SMS when I am next so that I can wait outside
As a receptionist, I want to skip a no-show so that the line keeps moving
A.competitive_analysis:
Paper tokens: free, no visibility
Qminder: powerful, expensive
WhatsApp groups: chaotic
A.competitive_quadrant:
quadrantChart
  title Cost vs Visibility
  x-axis Cheap --> Expensive
  y-axis Opaque --> Transparent
  "Paper": [0.1,0.1]
  "Qminder": [0.9,0.9]
  "Our Target Product": [0.2,0.85]
A.requirement_analysis: Hard part is the wait-time estimate; everything else is CRUD plus one SMS webhook.
A.requirement_pool:
P0 token issue
P0 live board
P0 SMS call-in
P1 phone tokens
P1 skip/recall
P2 per-doctor routing
P2 daily report
A.ui_design_draft: Kiosk: one big 'Take token' button. Board: now-serving + next 5. Phone: token + live position.
A.anything_unclear: Multiple doctors? → assume one queue in v1.

B.implementation_approach: Next.js App Router, server actions for mutations, SSE for the board, Twilio webhook for SMS status.

adrs.title: ADR-001 SSE over WebSockets
adrs.decision: One-way board updates; SSE is simpler and works through the clinic's proxy.

adrs.title: ADR-002 Twilio for SMS
adrs.decision: Reliable delivery receipts; cost acceptable at clinic volume.
